notes: **Bằng means "by/with" in the sense of a tool**, and that's the word for transport: *đi **bằng** xe máy* (go by motorbike), *viết **bằng** bút* (write with a pen), *nói **bằng** tiếng Việt* (speak in Vietnamese). The question is *đi bằng gì?* — "how are you getting there?".

**In everyday speech, *bằng* is often dropped**: *đi xe máy*, *đi taxi*, *đi bộ*. What you can't drop is the *bằng* in the question *đi bằng gì?*, because without it the sentence becomes *đi gì?*, which sounds like "go what?".

**Mất means "take" for time and "lose" for things.** *Mất bao lâu?* = "how long does it take?"; *mất hai tiếng* = "it takes two hours". The same word in *tôi bị mất ví* means "I lost my wallet" — and it really is one word, used both ways.

**Tắc đường (north) and kẹt xe (south) both mean "traffic jam".** You'll hear them constantly, usually in the full sentence *Hôm nay tắc đường quá!* — "the traffic is terrible today!". At rush hour in Hà Nội and Sài Gòn, that's no small talk.

**Xuống means "go down / get off" and lên means "go up / get on"** — for vehicles and for stairs alike. *Anh xuống ở đâu?* (where are you getting off?), *lên xe đi!* (get on, let's go!). For motorbikes and bicycles you'll hear *lên xe* / *xuống xe*; for planes and trains, *lên máy bay*, *xuống tàu*.

**Rồi sao nữa? means "and then?"** and it's what the driver will say every time you give a direction. Have your answers ready in short chunks — one instruction per sentence — because long directions are almost never understood while someone is driving.

grammars.title: Vehicles and bằng
body: Every vehicle uses the word *xe* (wheeled vehicle) as its head, followed by a description. Once again the order is building blocks: the thing described comes first, the description after it.
after: ⚠️ ***Xe ôm* literally means "hug vehicle"** — a motorbike taxi, named after the way passengers hold on. Most have now moved to apps (*Grab*, *Be*), but the word and the street-corner stands are still everywhere, and for short trips they're often faster.
*Tàu* on its own means both ship and train; the add-on tells them apart: *tàu hoả* (train), *tàu thuỷ* (ship). At A1, just remember *tàu* = train, since that's the most common use.

grammars.title: Giving directions
body: These eight sentences are enough to guide a driver anywhere. Say them one at a time, short, and don't string them together.

head: Tiếng Việt
Say it
Meaning
rows: Đến ngã tư thì rẽ phải
Dến ngã tư thì zẽ fải
Đến ngã ba thì rẽ trái
Dến ngã ba thì zẽ chái

after: ⚠️ In southern Vietnam *rẽ* is replaced by ***quẹo***: *quẹo phải*, *quẹo trái*. Both are understood everywhere, but if you're in Sài Gòn and the driver hesitates, try the other word.
*Lại* after a verb means "back" or "again": *quay lại* (turn around), *dừng lại* (stop), *làm lại* (redo), *nói lại* (say again). One small word that turns up everywhere.

blocks.text: ⚠️ *Anh bật đồng hồ nhé* — "please turn on the meter" — is a lifesaver for foreigners taking an ordinary taxi. Said kindly at the start of the ride, it spares you an unpleasant haggle at the end. *Đồng hồ* literally means "clock", and it's used for both the meter and a watch.
This isn't grammar, but it's one of the skills you'll need soonest — and the rules go against most newcomers' instincts.

blocks.title: Three rules for crossing
items: **Walk slowly and steadily**; don't stop and don't run. Riders calculate where you'll be one second from now and swing around behind you. Stopping suddenly ruins their calculation — that's what's dangerous, not the walking.
**Don't wait for the road to be empty**, because at rush hour it never will be. Wait for a small gap, then go and don't step back. Raising your hand to chest height makes you more visible.
**Cars and buses are a different story** — they won't swerve around you. Give way to anything with four wheels, and cross only between motorbikes.

blocks.text: ⚠️ *Mũ bảo hiểm* (helmet) is compulsory in Vietnam for motorbike riders and passengers alike, and the police really do fine people. Every ride-hailing driver carries a spare helmet; if he forgets, just say *Anh cho em mũ bảo hiểm với.*
